stop_condition: Every round-4 finding is either verified resolved by measurement or re-filed with fresh evidence, and no critical/high finding remains in green_check_run's timed_out inference, its QA_TRACKING_DIR precondition, or green-check.test.sh's two arm-forcing mechanisms.

findings.evidence: THE NARROWED CLAIM IS NARROWER AND STILL NOT TRUE, MEASURED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS. Shipped --help (rendered via `bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh --help | nl -ba | sed -n '615,640p'`) reads: 'a command that runs to EXACTLY the cap and then exits 124 on its own reads as a false positive on this path ... A command that exits 124 at any point BEFORE the cap is correctly reported as timed_out=false.' MEASUREMENT 1, shipped green_check_run (extracted verbatim, `awk 'NR>=13315 && NR<=13473' qa-gate.sh`) under the spec's own shim (extracted verbatim, `awk 'NR>=185 && NR<=207' green-check.test.sh`), start-fraction controlled via python3, cap=3 throughout, every run finishing STRICTLY BEFORE the cap: sleep 2.5 at frac .062 -> false; at frac .066 -> false; at frac .914 -> TRUE; at frac .915 -> TRUE; sleep 2.1 at frac .966 -> TRUE (0.9s of headroom, 30 percent of the budget, read as a cap fire). MEASUREMENT 2 isolates the arithmetic from the shim entirely -- bare `date +%s` pairs, no green_check_run, no shim: cap=3, real 2.5 at frac 0.05 -> elapsed 2 -> false; real 2.5 at frac 0.95 -> elapsed 3 -> CAP FIRED; real 2.1 at frac 0.95 -> elapsed 3 -> CAP FIRED; real 2.02 at frac 0.99 -> elapsed 3 -> CAP FIRED. So the defect is the shipped predicate's own clock, not the test apparatus. MECHANISM: elapsed = floor(T0+d) - floor(T0) = floor(f+d) where f is the start instant's sub-second fraction; R4-F3 correctly proved truncation cannot UNDERCOUNT a genuine cap-fire, and the unstated converse is the defect -- floor(f+d) can EXCEED floor(d), so a sub-cap run can measure AT the cap. Real-duration false-positive window is (cap-1, cap], one full second wide, probability equal to f. THE IMPLEMENTER MEASURED THE COUNTEREXAMPLE AND READ IT AS NOISE: green-check.test.sh:648-652 records 'this exact case at cap=3/sleep=2 read elapsed=3 on a loaded host, flipping this assertion' -- a 2-second run measuring elapsed=3 at cap=3 IS the counterexample to the sentence written three surfaces away in the same round; it was attributed to load and the margin was widened. WATCHDOG HALF RE-CONFIRMED FAIR: the 'EXACT on the watchdog path' clause is true (round-4 measurement: kill -TERM yields wait status 143, kill -KILL 137, self `exit 124` yields 124, so the marker file really is the only route to a forced 124 there).
findings.description: THE ROUND-4 REPAIR MADE THE FALSE CLAUSE STRONGER, NOT WEAKER. R4-F1's blocked wording was 'a command that calls exit 124 on its own, WELL INSIDE the cap, reports timed_out=false'. The rewrite dropped 'well inside' and substituted the absolute 'at any point BEFORE the cap', which is measurably false across a one-second window. The clause now stands on FIVE surfaces (--help, region header, function header, the spec's own header comment, run-tests.sh's comment) where it stood on four. SEPARATELY, THE REGION HEADER MISSTATES WHAT R4-F3 ACCOMPLISHED, qa-gate.sh:13229: 'a command that exits 124 at any point BEFORE the cap is now correctly NOT reported as a timeout, which it was not before this fix once inside the tolerance's one-second window.' Precisely: the OLD predicate's window was about (cap-2, cap] (one second deterministic plus one second probabilistic); the NEW one is about (cap-1, cap] (one second probabilistic). THE FIX HALVED THE WINDOW. It did not close it and it did not reduce it to 'exactly at the cap'. That is a claim about the change itself, sitting in the audit trail. HARM, SCOPED HONESTLY: identical to R4-F1's -- result=red either way so no gate decision changes, but an agent reading the shipped contract and seeing timed_out=true concludes the deadline fired and raises GREEN_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S or retries, for a suite that exited 124 on its own. That is exactly the misdiagnosis R3-F1 exists to prevent, and it is proportionally worse at small caps -- which is what an operator debugging with --help open is using (this spec's own sections use 2, 3 and 8). SEVERITY -- ARBITRATED HIGH BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, UPHELD, REASONING RECORDED SO THE NEXT READER SEES IT RATHER THAN THE VERDICT: (1) a repair that increases a claim's REACH while leaving it untrue is worse than the thing it repaired -- 'well inside the cap' is vague and arguably survivable, 'at any point BEFORE the cap' is absolute and false; (2) fifth consecutive round of this class at this same surface, and at some point the pattern IS the severity; (3) QA's own harm analysis applies unchanged from R4-F1, which was rated HIGH -- same reader, same wrong action. QA had flagged that a MEDIUM rating on window size (one second of a 540s default) would not be unreasonable; the disagreement is recorded rather than silently resolved, and it did not change the outcome because the repair is cheap either way. BINDING REPAIR -- ONE CLAUSE CARRYING THE REAL BOUND, ON ALL FIVE SURFACES, NOT A SOFTENING: state the window. For example: 'On the timeout/gtimeout path timed_out is an inference from rc=124 plus elapsed wall time, measured with whole-second date +%s readings at both ends. Because both ends truncate, a run whose real duration falls anywhere in (cap-1, cap] can measure at the cap: a self-inflicted 124 in the final second before the deadline reads as a false positive, with probability equal to the start instant's sub-second fraction. Only a 124 landing more than one second before the cap is guaranteed to read false.' KEEP the 'exact on the watchdog path' clause; that half is true. NO CODE CHANGE IS REQUIRED OR WANTED: -ge cap is the correct predicate (a genuine fire measures cap or cap+1, so -gt cap would MISS fires) and bash 3.2 on macOS has no portable sub-second clock. This is a text-only repair.

findings.evidence: THE DISCLOSED CO-LOCATION ASSUMPTION IS UNSAFE, ESTABLISHED BY SIMULATION PLUS A DISCRIMINATING SECOND RUN. This host cannot test the direction that matters (`command -v timeout gtimeout` returns nothing, rc=1), so I first established what CAN be established here: running the shipped build_path_without_timeout (extracted verbatim, `awk 'NR>=218 && NR<=232'`) against this host's live PATH returns a value BYTE-IDENTICAL to PATH -- the filter is a provable NO-OP here, and Sections 10/11 run the watchdog arm for exactly the pre-fix reason (this host lacks the binary). Then I built the layout the assumption denies: one directory holding `timeout` AND `date`, `jq`, `ps`, `sleep`, `mktemp`, `bash` -- i.e. /usr/bin -- and ran the SHIPPED filter against it. Result: PATH_NO_TIMEOUT retains only the fixture bin; timeout, gtimeout, date, jq, ps, sleep and mktemp are ALL GONE. Then I ran SECTION 10.1'S EXACT INVOCATION SHAPE under it: `PATH=$PATH_NO_TIMEOUT GREEN_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S=2 bash $QG green-check tid --phase after` -> rc=127, stdout 'command not found: bash'. 10.1 asserts rc=0 and .dispatch=watchdog; it gets 127 and non-JSON. THE STEP THAT TURNS A PLAUSIBLE OBJECTION INTO AN ESTABLISHED ONE: I re-ran with jq, bd and bash ARTIFICIALLY PRESERVED and everything else filtered, to prove the finding does not hinge on jq's location -> rc=2, 'qa-gate.sh: line 536: dirname: command not found', and an envelope carrying error_key=design_binding_unreadable -- a wrong error_key manufactured by a broken toolchain. Every Section 10/11 assertion still fails. And with a real timeout in /usr/local/bin but date/sleep/ps in /usr/bin, the test command `sleep 20` itself would not resolve. REACHABILITY IS THIS REPO'S OWN CI, BY LINE NUMBER: .github/workflows/test.yml:114 `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and :263 `run: bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh`. On Ubuntu, timeout is coreutils in /usr/bin, /bin is a usrmerge symlink to /usr/bin, and jq/date/sleep/ps/bash all live there -- both PATH entries are filtered. SECOND TRIGGER, ONE COMMAND FROM THIS BOX: `brew install coreutils` puts gtimeout in /opt/homebrew/bin, which is where this host's jq already lives (`command -v jq` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/jq).
findings.description: PATH_NO_TIMEOUT INVERTS THE PURPOSE OF THE FIX THAT INTRODUCED IT. R4-F2's repair was 'make BOTH arms run on EVERY host'. The shim half achieves that and is verified (see the R4-F2 ruling in llm_observations). The FILTER half achieves the opposite in the only direction it was written for: on a host WITHOUT timeout it does nothing at all, and on a host WITH timeout it breaks roughly fourteen assertions in Sections 10 and 11. There is no host class on which it does what green-check.test.sh:212-216 and run-tests.sh:713-717 say it does. THE SELF-CHECK CANNOT CATCH THIS, BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THIS IS THE REUSABLE SHAPE: 10.0 asserts only that timeout and gtimeout fail to resolve under PATH_NO_TIMEOUT -- a condition satisfied MOST STRONGLY by the pathological case, in which the entire directory was removed. On ubuntu-latest, 10.0 PASSES while 10.1 onward fail. A NON-VACUITY CHECK THAT THE FAILURE MODE SATISFIES IS NOT A NON-VACUITY CHECK. This is not 'the test is vacuous'; it is 'the test's guard is satisfied by the defect', and it is worth naming as its own shape. ALSO: the currently-running L1 tier structurally cannot detect this, because it runs on this host where the filter is a measured no-op -- which is why the coordinator stopped that tier at 15 of 63 (0 failures, 0 canary, floor NEVER written; PARTIAL, not a pass). BINDING REPAIR, BOTH HALVES, AND IT IS THE ALLOWLIST, NOT A PATCHED DENYLIST: (1) DENYLISTING A DIRECTORY TO REMOVE ONE BINARY CANNOT BE MADE CORRECT -- that is the structural statement, and it is why a smarter filter is not an option. Build a fixture directory of symlinks to every tool the run needs (bash jq bd date sleep ps mktemp dirname basename sed awk grep tr cat rm mkdir git sort head tail wc cmp chmod), resolved via `command -v` BEFORE filtering, EXCLUDING timeout/gtimeout, and set PATH to just that directory. (2) Add the filter's OWN negative control, the check whose absence let this ship: after building PATH_NO_TIMEOUT, assert that every tool in that list STILL RESOLVES under it. Pair it with the existing legs -- 10.1 and 11.x already observe the shipped artifact running -- per .claude/tests/README.md section 'The pairing requirement'.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:13693 (the mkdir guard); consequences at :13699-13710 and :13735; residual disclosed at .claude/scripts/tests/green-check.test.sh:731-736
findings.evidence: MEASURED AGAINST THE SHIPPED green_check_run WITH A DISCRIMINATING CONTROL, three cases. CASE 1, directory EXISTS but chmod 500: `mkdir -p` on it returns rc=0 -- the shipped guard's own predicate, so the guard does NOT fire -- and green_check_run returns '1 watchdog false'; the log file does not exist; a sentinel file the command would have written is ABSENT, so the command NEVER RAN. CASE 2, CONTROL, the same directory writable: green_check_run returns '0 watchdog false' and the sentinel IS written, so the probe discriminates and is not measuring a general failure to run. CASE 3, directory MISSING and parent unwritable -- the case the fix DOES close: `mkdir -p` returns rc=1 and the refusal fires. Reading the shipped caller forward from case 1's triple: :13699-13710 turns rc=1 into result=red and exit_code=1 with timed_out=false, and :13735's `[ -f $log_path ]` is false so NO log tail is emitted -- a suite that never ran, reported as a red one, with no evidence, in exactly the state where a reader most needs it.
findings.description: THE FIX CLOSES THE SUB-CASE R4-F4 DID NOT MEASURE AND LEAVES LIVE THE SUB-CASE IT DID. R4-F4's own evidence block reads 'Log directory present but NOT writable (chmod 500)' -- the finding's measured case is the one that remains open. REACHABILITY COMPARISON: .claude/.qa-tracking EXISTS in every installed project (post-edit.sh and `qa-gate.sh enter` create it), so 'existing directory' is the normal state and 'missing directory' is the exception; the fix covers the exception. QA'S OWN ROUND-4 ERROR, STATED PLAINLY AND RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN ONLY IN CHAT: I prescribed the idiom at qa-gate.sh:8732 as a BINDING repair without checking that it covered the case my own probe had measured. The implementer followed that instruction literally and disclosed the gap honestly in both the code comment and green-check.test.sh:731-736. The disclosure is accurate and I credit it; the instruction was mine and it was under-specified against my own evidence. SEVERITY HELD AT MEDIUM, matching R4-F4's own rating and R3-F3's precedent -- environmental trigger, same consequence, not an escalation. THIS ALONE WOULD NOT BLOCK. BINDING REPAIR, SMALL: keep the mkdir guard and add the writability check the idiom does not carry -- after `mkdir -p` succeeds, refuse on a failed `: > $log_path`, which is the exact operation that fails, under the same tracking_dir_unwritable error_key. Section 14 then needs a SECOND leg for the existing-but-unwritable case: mkdir the .qa-tracking directory FIRST, then chmod 500 it. Section 14.1's current shape (rm -rf .qa-tracking; chmod 500 .claude) is deliberately the other case and should stay.

findings.evidence: THE FIGURE IS WRONG AND ITS CAUSAL EXPLANATION IS INVERTED. The comment states 'a static grep of assert_eq call sites reads 113, not 115, the SAME static-undercounts-runtime gap this file has already documented for this exact spec once before.' Measured against .claude/scripts/tests/green-check.test.sh: `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*assert_eq '` = 112; `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*assert_contains '` = 4; `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*assert_(eq|contains) '` = 116; `grep -c 'assert_eq'` = 113. So 113 is `grep -c 'assert_eq'` -- it COUNTS THE FUNCTION DEFINITION `assert_eq() {` as a call site AND DROPS the four assert_contains sites. The correct static call-site count is 116. AND THE DIRECTION IS BACKWARDS: 116 static EXCEEDS 115 runtime because exactly one assertion is host-gated -- green-check.test.sh:407, `if command -v timeout`, gating 8.6, measured as the single remaining host-conditional leg (`grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*if .*command -v (g)?timeout'` returns that one line, and `awk 'NR>=407 && NR<=412' | grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*assert_'` returns 1). 116 - 1 = 115. The static grep OVERCOUNTS runtime on this host and would match it exactly (116) on a host with a real timeout -- the very host class R5-F2 shows this file cannot currently pass on.
findings.description: A COMMENT BLOCK THAT EXISTS TO CATCH DRIFT, DRIFTING THREE ROUNDS RUNNING, IS ITSELF THE FINDING. This is the THIRD CONSECUTIVE ROUND in which a number in this block was wrong: R3-F5 (57 standing while 67 shipped), R4-F2 (88 presented as host-independent while covering only one of two arms), and now 113. Per the project standing that every number carries the command that produced it, this one carries none, and no command a reader would plausibly write reproduces it as a call-site count. CREDIT WHERE DUE, EXPLICITLY: the AUTHORITATIVE figure (115, from the spec's own Total line) is correct on this host; the comment does say 'on this host today'; and the per-section arm attribution that R4-F2's binding repair demanded is present and accurate. The defect is the aside and its causal sentence. BINDING REPAIR: correct 113 to 116 with the command that produces it, and replace the 'static-undercounts-runtime' explanation with the real cause -- one host-gated assertion at :407 (8.6), so 116 static minus 1 skipped equals 115 runtime on a host lacking timeout, and 116 on a host that has one.

findings.evidence: MEASURED: the spec's shim TERM/KILLs only the wrapper it forked, not the process tree. Driving the extracted shim directly -- `timeout 2s bash -c 'sleep 25; echo leak-probe-marker'` -> rc=124 -- and looking one second later shows a surviving `sleep 25` reparented to ppid 1. 13.A sets test_cmd to 'sleep 20; echo should-not-finish', BYTE-IDENTICAL to 10.1's, which is the exact string 10.3 greps for via `pgrep -f 'sleep 20; echo should-not-finish'`.
findings.description: A NEW CONCURRENCY-FLAKE VECTOR INTRODUCED BY SECTION 13 REUSING SECTION 10's COMMAND STRING. Sequentially within one run this is safe (10.3 precedes 13.A). Across two CONCURRENT runs of the spec -- the shape that occurred repeatedly during this arc -- instance A's 13.A orphan can still be alive when instance B reaches 10.3, producing a false FAIL on an assertion that is otherwise sound. This is NOT a defect in the shipped code: a real GNU timeout behaves the same way without --kill-after/--foreground, and the shim is faithful to it. REPAIR IS ONE WORD: make 13.A's command textually distinct from 10.1's.

findings.evidence: 13.C now runs at cap=8 over 'sleep 3; exit 124' -- a five-second margin. Under the OLD predicate `elapsed >= cap-1 = 7`, elapsed 3 still yields false, so 13.C stays GREEN against the unfixed code and is a duplicate of 13.D rather than a regression test for R4-F3. Applying the standing 'would reverting the fix turn it red' check: for 13.C the answer is NO. The only leg that goes red against the unfixed state is 13.C-STATIC at :667-676, a grep of the shipped source text.
findings.description: THE DESIGN IS CORRECT; ONLY THE CREDIT IS WRONG, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS. Given R5-F1, a behavioural leg at the exact cap-1 boundary is inherently probabilistic, so a static leg IS the honest instrument, and green-check.test.sh:643-654 says exactly that in the spec itself. I am ruling the choice correct and NOT asking for a flaky boundary test. The defect is only that run-tests.sh:723 states 'case C plus a timing-independent static grep prove the R4-F3 fix' -- case C proves nothing about R4-F3. BINDING REPAIR: drop the credit to case C; attribute the R4-F3 proof to 13.C-STATIC alone, and say why a behavioural leg at the boundary is deliberately not attempted.
